thesis: A wide-moat, unlevered payments network with operating margin at a 2-year high and a strong uptrend, bought on trend strength and a low position in its own multiple range rather than a mechanical discount.
reason: The scorecard gives 4: top quality, a near-unlevered balance sheet, a wide moat and trend strength, with the FCF dip explained by litigation cash. It does not score on value: the expected value sits near the price and the de-rating risk is real. That supports only the standard core size, which Python volatility-scales. No cap is breached, so nothing is replaced.

triggers.text: TTM ROIC falls below 80%, giving up most of the five-year rise to 91.0% and signalling network pricing erosion.
TTM operating margin falls below 56%, reversing the five-year expansion from 54.4% to 60.1%.
TTM FCF margin falls below 40%, showing the cash gap is structural rather than litigation timing.
A final US rule, court decision or law (e.g. the Credit Card Competition Act) materially caps credit interchange or forces network routing choice.
